name: Vori
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: Glottolog lists only wordlists (Williamson Benue-Congo lists), sociolinguistic and ethnographic works; no grammar/phonology of Vori (Surubu) exists

sources.citation: rogerblench.info /Language/Niger-Congo/BC/Kainji/East Kainji/ directory listing, Internet Archive copy 2024-07-24, plus the Internet Archive's index of all rogerblench.info PDFs
sources.note: No Vori folder or file was ever posted (sub-folders Boze, Gbiri, General, Map, Moro, Panawa, Sheni, Tunzu only); no archived rogerblench.info URL contains Vori/Srubu/Surubu. The domain is now a casino site.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2020. The East Kainji languages of Central Nigeria. Afrika und Übersee 93: 45-70. DOI 10.15460/auue.2020.93.1.210
sources.note: Vori (=Srubu) appears in Table 1 (status 'Vigorous', source 'Blench (2016)' survey data) and the tree; sec. 3.1 phonology treats Boze tones (four levels) and says other East Kainji languages have reduced tone systems (tiMap two tones + rising; Shimizu H/L/downstep). No Vori prosody; the word 'stress' does not occur.

sources.citation: Decker, Ken & Benard Abraham. 2022. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the Rishiwa and Kizamani (Shuwa-Zamani [ksa]) Languages of Kaduna State, Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2022-024. Dallas: SIL International. 53 pp. (Glottolog ref 656701)
sources.note: Sec. 8.3 pp.18-19 (PDF 24-25) gives a second-hand summary of Blench's unpublished 2016 Vori ms: consonants (kp, gb, a retroflex, palatalization/labialization), eight vowels, and 'Blench (2016:1) discusses the possibility that there may be vowel lengthening in Vori and observes that it may be associated with a low-high tone sequence.' Vori forms are cited with tone marks (e.g. dì-kwàŋ 'stone'). Appendix E p.35: transcriptions preliminary, 'no in-depth analysis of tones'. Nothing on stress or accent (0 a full-text search for stress/accent hits).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2019/2020. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, ed. IV. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. Entry 472 Vori.
sources.note: Names (TiVori, PiVori/AVori, Srubu, Skrubu, Surubu, Zurubu, Fiti), location, classification, 'Source(s) Blench (2016)'; no Refs line (no grammar, phonology or dictionary listed). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2018. Nominal affixing in the Kainji languages of northwestern and central Nigeria. In Watters (ed.), East Benue-Congo, 59-106. Berlin: Language Science Press.
sources.note: 'Vori (=Surubu)' only in the East Kainji tree figure; nothing on its phonology.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger & Stuart McGill. 2012. The Kainji languages of northwestern and central Nigeria (circulation draft).
sources.note: Surubu appears in a language list only; tone sections concern West Kainji languages (Cinda, Hungworo). Nothing on Vori.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2004ff. The status of the East Kainji languages of Central Nigeria: recent research (ms, rogerblench.info)
sources.note: Surubu listed in the Kauru cluster and in the 'arm, hand' appendix (ka-tSara, from BCCW). Nothing on Vori prosody.
Cites Blench 2016 'Weeping over the disappearance..' presentation and the Atlas; no phonology.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2016. The Vori [Srubu] language of Central Nigeria and a guide to writing. Unpublished ms (Kay Williamson Educational Foundation / SIL Nigeria survey, Jos).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only first-hand phonology of Vori known to exist (vowels, tone, consonants, morphophonemics on pp.1-2 per Decker & Abraham 2022); if any prosody/stress statement exists for Vori it is here. Obtainable only from Blench or SIL Nigeria (Luther Hon).
